paper.title: Optimal Regret Analysis of Thompson Sampling in Stochastic Multi-armed Bandit Problem with Multiple Plays

settings.name_in_paper: Multiple-play MAB (MP-MAB) problem with Bernoulli rewards
settings.definition_quote: Let there be $K$ arms. Each arm $i \in [K]$ is associated with a probability distribution $\nu_i = \Bernoulli(\mu_i)$, $\mu_i \in (0,1)$. At each round $t=1,2,\dots,T$, the forecaster selects a set of $L < K$ arms $I(t)$, then receives the rewards of the selected arms. ... \Regret(T)=\sum_{t=1}^T (\sum_{i \in [L]} \mu_i - \sum_{i \in I(t)} \mu_i).

bound.regime: for any sufficiently small eps_1 > 0, eps_2 > 0

symbols.Delta_iL: mu_L - mu_i, gap between suboptimal arm i and the L-th (m-th) best arm
symbols.C_a: constant independent of T, O(eps_1^-2) for fixed means
symbols.C_b: function of T that grows as O(log log T) for a proper choice of eps_2
symbols.m: number of arms selected per round (paper's L)

conditions: all arms have distinct means (or more generally the L-th arm's mean is distinct: mu_{L-1} > mu_L > mu_{L+1})
tuning: uniform Beta(1,1) prior on each arm
eps_2 = O(log log T / log T) in the analysis gives C_b = O(log log T)

source.label: thm:mainregret
source.quote: For any sufficiently small $\epsilonOne>0, \epsilon_2>0$, the regret of MP-TS is upper-bounded as \Expect[\Regret(T)] \leq \sum_{i \in \subopts} \left( \frac{(1+\epsilonOne) \Delta_{i,L} \log{T}}{d(\mu_i, \mu_L)} \right) + C_a(\epsilonOne, \mu_1,\mu_2,\dots,\mu_K) + C_b(T, \epsilon_2, \mu_1,\mu_2,\dots,\mu_K), where, $C_a$ is a constant independent on $T$ and is $O(\epsilonOne^{-2})$ ... $C_b$ ... grows at a rate of $O(\log \log{T}) = o(\log{T})$.

results.notes: Paper's L is m. Regret defined through means, so pseudo-regret. By setting eps_1 = O((log T)^{-1/3}), the paper derives E[Reg] <= sum_{i>L} Delta_{i,L} log T / d(mu_i,mu_L) + O((log T)^{2/3}), matching Anantharam et al.'s lower bound asymptotically; it also notes asymptotic high-probability optimality. The algorithm does not use T, but the analysis choice of eps_2 depends on T.
